worst_errors: p-raycap-north-charleston-sc:production_type: a company-wide product statement ('Raycap's goal is ... STEALTH poles ... customizable based on the location') is presented as the North Charleston plant's production type. Corrected to inferred. p-ehresmann-yankton-sd:certifications: the value 'AISC' reads as a registry certification, but the AISC certified-company directory has no Ehresmann row (only EEI Enterprise, LLC, Yankton). Corrected to the company's own claim. The opening line states the certification as fact.

p-raycap-north-charleston-sc:products: the second clause (concealed small cell and STEALTH poles) is taken from the company-goal sentence, not from text naming the plant. Corrected to the plant-naming text (steel fabrication/integration and composite/concealment facilities, STEALTH line).
opening_line_problems: p-ehresmann-yankton-sd: 'Ehresmann Engineering in Yankton is certified by the American Institute of Steel Construction' states AISC certification as fact. Only the company's own site says so; the AISC directory snapshot lists EEI Enterprise, LLC (Yankton) and not Ehresmann. Reword to 'says it is certified by AISC'.

p-raycap-north-charleston-sc: the second clause ('and that its STEALTH poles are customizable based on the location') rests on p-raycap-north-charleston-sc:production_type, now corrected to inferred (company-level). The clause is accurately attributed to the release but is not a plant-level stated fact; consider dropping it or keeping only the 112,000 sq ft facility clause.
No opening line among the 8 plants asserts a current Path deployment. The other 6 lines (Larwel, Browning, Stony Brook, Metal Pros, Pelco, Hurtt) use only stated claims for their plants.
score_problems: p-raycap-north-charleston-sc:score_part_mix 15: its only cited claim (production_type) is now inferred (company-level statement). Points can stay at the custom level only if the coordinator accepts the inference. In either case confidence drops from 2 to 1.

p-raycap-north-charleston-sc:score_scale 5: the reasoning says 'multi-site parent' but cites only p-raycap-north-charleston-sc:headcount (unknown rows). No cited claim establishes a multi-plant parent. Support exists: raycap.com/company lists plants in Germany, Greece, Slovenia, Kearny NJ, Post Falls ID and three in North Charleston. Add a parent/multi-plant claim and cite it. Lead, not evidence: search results show 2026 Raycap plant-manager postings citing about 300 plant employees, which would make scale 10 if confirmed from a fetchable page.

p-hurtt-marceline-mo:score_scale and p-stony-brook-calverton-ny:score_scale cite '<id>:headcount', but no headcount evidence row exists for either plant. The points (0) are right but the citations point to missing rows.

Part mix scored inconsistently: Larwel scores 8 (mixed) for 'TxDOT-standard plus custom'. Stony Brook's own text is 'One offs or production runs', and Browning's quoted sentence continues 'From prototype to mass production' (cut from the ledger quote), yet both score 15. Both are arguably the mixed level (8). Flag for the coordinator to decide. If changed, Stony Brook goes 23 to 16 and Browning 23 to 16.

p-metal-pros-wichita-ks:welder_postings has two evidence rows: a stale 'none found' (unknown) and the stated '1 open: Welder (ALL SHIFTS)'. score_labor 12 matches the stated row; retire the stale row.

Stale reasoning text: the material reasoning for Raycap ('scored 12 per ledger precedent'), Pelco ('rubric level 12 applied as a fallback'), Browning, Metal Pros and Ehresmann ('suited to Rove') still describes the old 12 level, although the value is correctly 0 under the run_log material rule (normalisation notes are appended). Rewrite the reasoning to say 'unknown part size = 0'.

p-hurtt-marceline-mo:materials is 'unknown (steel not stated)' in the ledger, but hurttfab.com/capabilities (already a source for this plant) states 'Products are manufactured using steel, stainless steel, and aluminum'. This is a missed stated fact that bears on the prospect test (it welds carbon/stainless steel). It does not change score_material_part (no part size). It is not counted in claims_checked because the row is tagged unknown.

Arithmetic and tiers checked for all 8 plants: totals equal the sum of components (Larwel 36, Raycap 28, Browning 23, Stony Brook 23, Metal Pros 35, Pelco 35, Ehresmann 23, Hurtt 23; all Low). Confidence values match the run_log rule (components above 0 whose cited claims are all stated), except Raycap after this correction. All other cited claim_ids exist. Rubric levels otherwise match CLAUDE.md as clarified (Larwel process 20 on stated MIG; Browning process 0 on SAW only; labor 12 for Metal Pros and Pelco on one undated open posting; Hurtt labor 0 for a standing resume invitation).

Raycap: 2026 North Charleston postings in search results. Browning: site and 2026 company blog. Stony Brook: AISC snapshot 2026-11-12 and MassDOT list. Pelco lead (not evidence): an IBISWorld SupplierIQ profile in search results lists 175 employees for Pelco Structural LLC. If fetched and quoted, score_scale would go from 0 to 5.
Ehresmann lead: a sister company, Needmore Towers, is named in a search-result profile; EEI Enterprises LLC shares the Yankton address. Common ownership is not established.
